sub_criteria.name: extraction accuracy
sub_criteria.text: Measures LLM claim-extraction accuracy from full papers or abstracts against expert/human annotation, ideally broken down by paper section, claim type, or model.

sub_criteria.name: evidence-link errors
sub_criteria.text: Characterizes how claim-to-evidence links (passage, table, or citation) fail: fabricated support, wrong-direction reads of contradicting evidence, or over-generalisation past the paper's conditions.

sub_criteria.name: benchmark construction
sub_criteria.text: Describes how a claim-evidence or citation-grounding benchmark (e.g. SciFact, CiteME, or similar) was built, and what its reported numbers can or cannot legitimately support.

sub_criteria.name: abstention and calibration
sub_criteria.text: Tests whether abstention or calibrated uncertainty improves the trustworthiness of extracted claims, and reports the coverage cost of doing so.

sub_criteria.name: cross-model or cross-domain generalisation
sub_criteria.text: Reports whether extraction or grounding results replicate across different models, domains, or paper types, or whether they are inflated by benchmark artifacts.

items.abstract_600: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in open-domain settings faces significant challenges regarding irrelevant information in retrieved documents and the alignment of generated answers with user intent. items.title: Evaluating the Factuality of Large Language Models Using Multiple Plug-and-Play Fact Sources
items.abstract_600: Large language models (LLMs) often produce factually inaccurate content, or hallucinations, which undermines their reliability. Existing factuality evaluation systems usually rely on a single predefined fact source, making them task-specific and hard to extend. We present UFO, a unified framework for factuality evaluation that supports multiple plug-and-play fact sources. UFO integrates human-written evidence, web search results, and LLM knowledge within a single evaluation pipeline, and allows users to flexibly select, reorder, and even define customized sources. items.title: Survey of machine learning techniques for Arabic fake news detection
items.abstract_600: Abstract Social media platforms have emerged as primary information sources, offering easy access to a wide audience. Consequently, a significant portion of the global population relies on these platforms for updates on current events. However, fraudulent actors exploit social networks to disseminate false information, either for financial gain or to manipulate public opinion. items.abstract_600: With the widespread application of large language models (LLMs) in natural language processing (NLP), hallucinations have become a significant impediment to their effective use of LLMs in industry applications. To address this challenge, we integrate existing hallucination detection and mitigation methods into a unified hallucination detection and mitigation framework. items.abstract_600: Despite their impressive ability to generate high-quality and fluent text, generative large language models (LLMs) also produce hallucinations: statements that are misaligned with established world knowledge or provided input context. However, measuring hallucination can be challenging, as having humans verify model generations on-the-fly is both expensive and time-consuming. items.abstract_600: Large language models (LLMs) can answer religious knowledge queries fluently, yet they often hallucinate and misattribute sources, which is especially consequential in Islamic settings where users expect grounding in canonical texts (Qur'an and Hadith) and jurisprudential (fiqh) nuance. items.abstract_600: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated excellent capabilities in Question Answering (QA) tasks, yet their ability to identify and address ambiguous questions remains underdeveloped. items.abstract_600: Effective memory is crucial for LLM agents, yet constructing it effectively remains challenging. items.abstract_600: Abstract Automated fact-checking systems verify claims against evidence to predict their veracity.
